round3_reason: Post-acceptance fix: BIO-OPS-003-AC04 round 2 (SY-OPS003-02, High, Kemi's ruling). See evidence/BIO-CRD-006/builder/metadata.json and docs/features/bio-crd-007/README.md's own 'Post-acceptance fix: BIO-OPS-003-AC04' section for the full cross-feature record. This story's own ProductionJobLockRegistry was never excluded from BIO-CRD-006's own concurrent read-then-activate - a new, decoupled ICardActivationBarrier interface (Domain/ICardActivationBarrier.cs) wraps a new SHARED, host-layer Biolog.Api.Cards.CardActivationBarrierLockRegistry (Emeka, commit 7b79866) that BOTH features' modules now adapt onto the SAME singleton. Every one of this story's six ProductionJobLockRegistry acquisition sites (CreateJobAsync, the shared RecordStepAsync serving print/encode/readback-QC, RejectJobAsync, CancelJobAsync, CompleteOfflineJobAsync, ActivateAfterProductionAsync) now also acquires the shared barrier immediately after, nested the same way - enforced as an invariant via a structural harness check comparing call counts, not naming each site, so a future 7th acquisition cannot silently escape the fix. Verified by a new real-packaged-host test proving a real POST .../production/jobs call genuinely blocks while the test holds the shared lock directly, then succeeds once released - the CRD-006-direction mutant check (documented in BIO-CRD-006's own evidence entry) independently confirms the harness has real discriminating power. Verified: dotnet build clean, feature tests 56/56 (unchanged count, existing constructors extended not replaced), full dotnet integration suite 295/295 (+2 new barrier tests shared with BIO-CRD-006), dotnet unit suite 211/211 (unaffected), structural harness 51/51 (46 pre-existing + 5 new checks).
